heroHeadline: COLBY TELLS RAMSTEIN-36 EUROPE MUST FUND AND LEAD UKRAINE'S DEFENSE, WARNS OF 'PROTRACTED WAR' (SEP 8); RUTTE DECLARES 'NATO 3.0' ALLIANCE'S BIGGEST SHIFT SINCE COLD WAR IN BERLIN (SEP 10); SEP 18 COLBY-EUCOM TROOP-OPTIONS BRIEFING STILL PENDING
heroSubtitle: As of September 11, 2026, the NATO-US tensions story advanced on two fronts this week: burden-sharing for Ukraine and the broader 'NATO 3.0' framework for shifting conventional-defense responsibility to Europe. At the 36th Ukraine Defense Contact Group meeting on September 8 — held virtually and co-chaired by Germany and the UK — Pentagon Under Secretary of War for Policy Elbridge Colby told the roughly 50-nation coalition that Washington 'cannot predict' when the war ends and that the burden of financing and arming Ukraine's defense must fall primarily on European partners, warning allies to prepare for a 'protracted war' and pointing to the PURL scheme (Europe pays for US-made arms) as the ongoing US contribution model. Partners pledged fresh contributions including UK, Dutch and Norwegian funding and contracts for roughly 1,000 additional Patriot interceptor missiles, even as Ukraine flagged an €8 billion gap against its stated needs. Two days later, on September 10, NATO Secretary General Rutte used Germany's Heads of Mission Conference in Berlin to call 'NATO 3.0' — the shift of primary conventional-defense responsibility to European allies and Canada while the US retains the nuclear backstop — 'the most profound transformation of the Alliance since the Cold War,' citing Germany's new Lithuania brigade and eastern-flank corps command as proof points, and reaffirmed NATO 'solidarity' with Germany following the alleged Russian hybrid attack on Leipzig airport. Neither statement addressed the Pentagon's Europe force-posture review directly; the September 18 decision briefing between the top US general in Europe and Colby, and the November 6 deadline for Hegseth's four troop-level options, remain the next concrete checkpoints.
